saints.name: St. Januarius
saints.title: Bishop and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The bishop of Benevento martyred under Diocletian, whose relic of blood is famously venerated at Naples…
biography: Januarius, in Naples San Gennaro, was Bishop of Benevento when the persecution of Diocletian fell upon the churches. According to his ancient passio he was arrested while visiting imprisoned Christians, thrown to the beasts in the amphitheatre of Pozzuoli, and at last beheaded about the year 305, together with the deacons Sossus, Festus, and Proculus and the lector Desiderius.

A pious woman is said to have gathered his blood into two ampoules, kept to this day in the treasury chapel of Naples cathedral, whither his body also was brought in 1497. Since at least 1389 the congealed blood has been seen to liquefy, thrice in the year: on his feast, 19 September; on the Saturday before the first Sunday of May; and on 16 December.

The Church permits the veneration without pronouncing on the marvel's nature. Principal patron of Naples, Januarius is invoked against the eruptions of Vesuvius, whose threatening in 1631 is held to have been stayed at his intercession, and his relic of blood has made him a patron of blood banks and their donors.
saints.knownFor: His martyrdom and the veneration of his blood-relic at Naples.
